newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania says foreign debt hit $10.9 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Romania says foreign debt hit $10.9 bln in 1996.

text.p: Romania's medium- and long- term foreign debt hit $10.916 billion in 1996, sharply up from end-September figures of $6.255 billion, the government said at the weekend.
Government spokesman Eugen Serbanescu announced the new debt figure, which contradicts previous data released by the former leftist cabinet.

"The real situation is much more difficult", he told a news conference, speaking about economic performance data reported by ex-President Ion Iliescu's leftists, ousted from office for the first time in seven years in elections last November.
Serbanescu could not explain the rise in the debt figure, double the end-1995 amount, saying that it did not include commercial loans without state guarantee.
Latest central bank (BNR) data put Romania's medium- and long-term foreign debt, including commercial debt, at $6.255 billion at end-September, when short-term liabilities were $728.5 million.
BNR officials were not available for comment on Sunday.
The new centrist coalition government has set foreign borrowings in 1997 at up to $3.2 billion, needed for investments, economic restructuring and to enhance Romania's hard currency reserves.

The central bank governor said last month that Romania's external debt limit would be about $3.0 billion this year, with BNR expected to raise medium- and long-term loans worth up to $1.5 billion from international markets.

Romania resumed syndicated loans in 1995, followed by its first Samurai and Eurobond issues last year. It got its first rating from major agencies -- a BB plus from Japan Credit Rating Agency, BB-minus by Standard and Poors and Britain's IBCA and BA-three by Moody's Investors Service.
The ratings were based, among other criteria, on a relatively low external debt level.
